nodes.title: BEIR: A Heterogenous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
limitations: Historical systems; retrieval metrics do not establish answer or forecast correctness.

nodes.title: Capability can reinforce control
nodes.statement: Capability gains may increase resources and access rights, which may support further capability growth.

nodes.title: Complete records do not establish the truth of verification claims
nodes.statement: The retained diagnosis reconciled 96 saved attempts without rerunning a candidate. Four of 22 eligible operative exactly bound claims disagreed with stipulated artifact validity across 22 cases; three of 21 positive claims accompanied invalid artifacts. Each compact method lost two observable opportunities through bounded retention; lossless controls recovered those opportunities but still accepted the three invalid deliveries. These are descriptive synthetic results, not real verifier error rates or independent causal proof.

nodes.title: Identical available evidence can conceal different actual rights
nodes.statement: The constructed baseline and late-revocation cases supplied identical candidate bytes and produced the same release proposal, although authority differed in the stipulated world. Each arm therefore retained one unauthorized proposal, which the common world-state guard refused. No duplicate or unauthorized effects were observed, but this guard conformance does not establish observer safety or a realizable distributed authorization service.

nodes.title: Equal development totals can conceal opposite retention losses
nodes.statement: In one owned twelve-case simulation, both 2048-byte views completed four of five observable opportunities and four of seven world opportunities, but missed opposite storage-pressure cases. Both lossless controls completed five of five observable opportunities. This is an exposed development comparison of full retention/view systems, not graph superiority, broad predictive capability or live exchange evidence.

nodes.title: Exchange must separate delivery and settlement
nodes.statement: Offer order, latency, service quality, payment and reputation should be represented and evaluated separately.

nodes.title: Authority checks leave delivery-quality errors visible
nodes.statement: Each of four fixed arms produced 3 accepted simulated releases for artifacts later stipulated invalid, despite 0 unauthorized and 0 duplicate effects. Positive observed verification and actual artifact quality were separate facts in these deliberately constructed cases. This records a limit of the declared guard and evidence contract, not an estimate of real verifier error prevalence.

nodes.title: Actions change prediction targets
nodes.statement: Using forecasts to select actions can alter the distribution of subsequent outcomes.

nodes.title: One first inventory passed a separately implemented check
nodes.statement: The first registered inventory of one committed theory document accounted for 20 supported links and 28 exclusions. A separate checker and non-producer review passed its original bytes; the producer claim agreed in one eligible delivery. This establishes one artifact’s scoped conformance, not general reliability, rendered navigation, predictive advantage or independent time assurance.

nodes.title: Separate clauses recover support under a larger selection budget
nodes.statement: Two fixed local repetitions returned identical ordered results. Discovery support was complete at five passages and commitment support at one. The union of both top-five lists covers the original complete bundles using ten distinct passages rather than five. A post-execution transport repair preserved the unchanged measurement core without new retrieval. The actual controller selected one offline control/exchange decision-pilot preparation. This visible development diagnostic is not an equal-budget quality improvement, adoption result, predictive advantage or business advantage.

nodes.title: Fresh scripted tradeoffs remain paired rather than aggregate gains
nodes.statement: One post-freeze 24-case scripted cohort produced 96 retained attempts. Both compact methods completed 7/9 observable and 7/11 world opportunities, with two successful releases unique to each method and net difference 0. Both lossless controls reached 9/9 observable and 9/11 world opportunities. This is a descriptive result for hand-designed mechanisms, not representative performance or superiority of graph notation.

nodes.title: Graph usefulness depends on task and budget
nodes.statement: Graph retrieval should be compared with strong text retrieval at matched context and total construction costs.

nodes.title: Historical-state retrieval needs its own provenance assessment
nodes.statement: Memento provides datetime negotiation and TimeMaps for prior resource states. In this project, an archive response would still require retained bytes, collection timing and separately assessed provenance before use as historical evidence; retrieval alone is not a complete knowledge snapshot.

nodes.title: Standards describe structure and provenance
nodes.statement: RDF, PROV-O, SHACL and nanopublications offer complementary interchange, provenance, validation and assertion packaging.

nodes.title: Operational meta-representation
nodes.statement: A meta-representation records representation families, permitted transformations, preservation obligations and comparative evidence.

nodes.title: Newer information is not automatically true
nodes.statement: Preserve disagreement and corrections separately instead of making recency the scientific truth policy.

nodes.title: Portability can distribute control
nodes.statement: Substitutable providers and portable representations may reduce dependence and concentrated veto rights.

nodes.title: A sufficient alternative differs from a required conjunction
nodes.statement: C4 defines support as all exact spans in at least one declared sufficient bundle. This gives each supported question one vote, accepts complete alternatives, and prevents partial alternatives from being combined into an undeclared answer. Semantic sufficiency still requires review; exact byte coverage does not prove answer correctness. The versioned definition is a measurement contract, not an empirical finding.

nodes.title: Two time axes are necessary
nodes.statement: World-time claims and collection-time eligibility must remain separate to prevent retrospective knowledge leakage.

nodes.title: Receipt inclusion, statement accuracy and issuance order are separate
nodes.statement: RFC 9943 distinguishes signed statements and registration receipts from factual accuracy. A relying party cannot assume registration sequence matches issuance order unless the service policy promises it, and selective issuer submission remains possible.

nodes.title: Existence proofs do not establish truth
nodes.statement: A verified timestamp can support prior existence of committed bytes without proving their truth or availability to a model.

limits: This is a reviewed public selection, not the complete research catalog. A citation does not certify that a claim is true.
External sources are bibliographic references; article bytes were not archived by this map. Publication and review dates are not collection receipts.
Claim status and basis are curator attributions. Observed local implementation or synthetic results do not establish predictive advantage or independent execution assurance.
Proposed experiment and representation nodes describe catalog concepts, not the completion status of associated runs. Challenges may describe qualifications or competing mechanisms.
The source commit and document digests identify retained local bytes. They are not independent timestamps or evidence of historical availability.
